messages.text: Papa Wanga's Poppet

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Ah, a hero! Welcome to Quartero's Curios!

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Come come, step right in, don't just stand there at the side of the road!

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Step into my emporium! Over on this other side of the road!

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: My name is Quartero! I am the proprietor of this establishment.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Or at least the small patch of roadside I've appropriated for that purpose.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Here, let me roll out some blankets so you can get a better look at my priceless treasures.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Can I offer you anything? I have a tin of sardines I was eating, would you like one?

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: No? Alright. Let's get down to business!

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: I shouldn't even do this, but what the hell.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: You see this little fellow? Yours. Free of charge. Just for being my first customer of the day.
Papa Wanga's Mask

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: May I be blunt? You look like a vagrant, dear.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: A heroic one, of course, in the wandering sense, but also, let's be clear, the homeless one.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Luckily, that's where yours truly comes in. Here, try this voodoo mask on.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Purely decorative. As long as you don't say any voodoo words over it. Then it WILL shrink your head.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: There. Now don't move. Let me look at you.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Oh, yes. Yes yes yes. That... looks... stunning!
Papa Wanga's Belt

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: I'm sure you've guessed by now: I don't sell pantaloons to farmers here.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: No, I provide the priceless to the truly exceptional.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Kings, conquerors, demigods... heroes like yourself.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Here, try this enormous bone phallus on.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Hm, yes. Yes, yes — on you it works. On you it works.
Papa Wanga's Backplate

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Now, I suspect you're wondering: given my frankly devilish appearance...

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: The fact that these items are clearly priceless...

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: The fact that I haven't even MENTIONED a price yet...

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: And the fact that we're standing at a crossroads at midnight...

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: What, in a nutshell, is the CATCH?

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Let me snug up that belt for you. There.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Yes. Yes, that backplate was made for you.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: That's a genuine person's skull wedged into it, by the way. I can't say whose, but someone VERY famous.
Papa Wanga's Basket

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: What's the catch, my dear hero? The catch is... that there IS no catch.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: So: one catch total.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Everything I'm offering you here tonight — including this handsome voodoo coconut basket — is free.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Not a string attached. I couldn't tie a single thread to this transaction if I tried.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Even a modest ten percent gratuity would trigger a sharp pain deep inside my bones. What do you call it... the marrow, I think?

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Yes, the marrow part would turn into boiling worms or something. It's happened several times, and let me assure you, it stings like you would not :hero_faceless_void::hero_undying::hero_crystal_maiden::hero_kunkka:ing believe.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: And therein lies my tragic yet riveting backstory.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Don't worry, here it comes.
Papa Wanga's Staff

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Here, let's add the staff. I'm going to step back, and turn around, and then pretend I'm seeing you for the first time with everything on. Okay, here we go.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Oh, that looks fantastic on you! I insist you abscond with the entire set.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: And as mentioned, put your money away. I will not —  CAN not — take a single solitary cent.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: As for that tale of woe I promised you, it's a doozy. A painful and frankly embarrassing memory for yours truly.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: In fact, I wouldn't burden you with it if I didn't technically HAVE—

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Well, we'll get to that.
Morrigan's Fury

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Could I trouble you to crouch a moment, darling? Let me get this Morrigan's Fury on you, and...

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: There. Snug as a button.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Where was I? Ah, my tragic backstory, yes. Brace yourself for pathos, this one's going to pluck at the heart strings a bit.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Once upon a time, in a fantastical world, much unlike the grounded world of realism we live in now, I was a member of a famous adventuring party!

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: We were fearless! Brazen! Reckless! Foolhardy! And if you sense these superlatives becoming less positive and beginning to nudge toward an inevitable and spectacular downfall...

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Don't worry, we're getting there.
Vengeful Spirit  - Titania's Fury Legs

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: No, I wasn't the tank holding the front line, or the marksman providing ranged support from behind.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Could I get you to lift a leg, dear? Feel free to steady yourself on my back, I'm sturdy as an oak. There, that's the Misery on.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: No, I was something even MORE important! And even FURTHER back! The QUARTERMASTER.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: The logistical mastermind maintaining the party's battle readiness with my invaluable skills in procurement, repairs, and strategic rationing. Leading the charge, from behind.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Castles, caves, dungeons! There was no quest that was too much for us! No obstacle that–

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Well, I can see your eyes starting to wander, so let's cut to the chase: obviously there WAS a quest that was too much for us, so let's spill the tea and get to it.
Vengeful Spirit - Titania's Fury Head

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Let's get this Morrigan's Measure on you. These are real Ostrivian swamp ostrich feathers, by the way. Or maybe it's Pellivian skybeaver. It's extinct, anyway.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Wandering back to my tragic tale. From the very start, nothing went right.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Behind every door, skeletons. Behind every secret passage, skeletons. Inside every treasure chest, skeletons.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: There should obviously be SOME skeletons, it was a dungeon, after all, but the skeleton-to-square-foot ratio here was absurd.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Then half of the party melted into the unknowable shadows.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: And of course there were skeletons there too, so we heard a lot of screaming from the unknowable shadows.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: More skeletons arrived, obviously. Everything went absolutely :hero_faceless_void::hero_abyssal_underlord::hero_chaos_knight::hero_kez:ing pear-shaped.
Vengeful Spirit - Titania's Fury Weapon

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Hold on, I know there's a weapon that comes with this, where did I — there it is. Morrigan's Malice!

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Watch out, it's sharp. Also glowing. I wouldn't let the glowy parts touch your skin if I were you, pick it up by the hilt. There you go.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Now, here's the wrinkle: Could I have brought them all back to full health with my bag of priceless tonics? Or given them a first-rate weapon, like that glowy number you're swinging around right now?

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Technically, yes. And more technically, they asked.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Can I be blunt? They weren't going to make it. There's a dungeon crawl, and then there's just crawling through a dungeon.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: So, to spare you the saga, yours truly wisely decided...

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: ...to hoard the supplies.
Drakon's Deed Gauntlets

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: The Drakon's Deed. You haven't taken your eyes off it since you got here.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Yes, it's free and yes, you can have it.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: But the Drakon's Deed is the jewel of my collection, so I hope you appreciate it.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: I'd never part with something this valuable if I wasn't being forced to at curse-point.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: I'm spoiling my own tragic backstory. Let me hurry this along before I give away any more twists.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: By the end, it was just me. And the boss monster of the dungeon. One of those vast incomprehensible eldritch horror things, you know the type.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Mouths where eyes should be and vice versa. I certainly wasn't going to fight the :hero_faceless_void::hero_ursa::hero_clinkz::hero_kunkka:ing thing.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: I was just heading for the door when... it stopped me.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: And GLOWERED at me with a thousand glowering eyeballs.
Drakon's Deed Helm

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: If you just lean forward slightly I can get this headpiece on you.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Woof, this feels like it weighs eighty pounds, that can't be good for the spine.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Anyway: boss monster, stopped me, glowering, eyeballs. I don't mind telling you, for an ancient eldritchian horror, he had some VERY strong words for yours truly about my approach to teamwork.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: He seemed to think I was some kind of greedy coward.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: He had me all wrong, of course, but he also had me wrapped up in his filthy tentacles at the bottom of his cave, so what was I supposed to do? At any rate, he CURSED me.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Well, he insisted it wasn't a curse. More of a moral rebuke.
Drakon's Deed Tassets

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: To cut a tragic tale short: Because of what he deemed my appalling greed and cowardice, I would never be able to keep anything valuable again.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: I am sentenced — doomed, really — to spend my life handing over all my best stuff — and I'm talking the really good shit here — to heroes like yourself.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Speaking of which, those knee plates are solid gold, so don't actually take a knee in them or you'll scuff the finish.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Hm. Yes, I hear the squeaking too. I'd just walk around in them a bit, you'll need to work the leather in.
Drakon's Deed Pauldrons

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: These pauldrons are solid bronze, by the way. If I had to guess, they couldn't weigh an ounce less than two hundred pounds.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Not a problem for a strapping hero like yourself, of course.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: But if you DO start to feel a crippling pain in the shoulders, I think it's a safe guess it's the pauldrons. Bring them back in, we can hollow some of that bronze out.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Where was I? Right. Cursed forevermore by a protoplasmic horror to give away all my stuff.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: And the worst part? Just so there's no mistaking any of this gift-giving for actual generosity...

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: I am ALSO condemned to explain the awkward origin of my predicament to anyone who asks.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Plus anyone who doesn't ask.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: WHICH I HAVE JUST DONE! In case any eldritch horrors are listening in like last time...
Drakon's Deed Banners

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: So there you have it. Quartero the Former Quartermaster's tragic past.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Condemned to give away priceless treasures to anyone who looks remotely heroic.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: And also doomed to share my frankly humiliating backstory, whether you ask for it or not.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Heartbreaking stuff. For me, obviously.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: You're making out like a bandit here. If a watchman spotted any of this he'd accuse you of highway robbery.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Speaking of which, how does that backpiece fit? That's real bronze, like the shoulders. Five hundred pounds, I'd bet. But you'll barely even feel the weight once you get moving in it.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Though I'd move around mostly in the shade if I were you, that bronze is going to get hot in the sun.
Drakon's Deed Lance

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Now we come to the piece de resistance: the Drakon's Deed Lance. What war ensemble would be complete without it?

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: WHSSH! FWSHH! PWSSH! Look at this thing cut the air!

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: A terrifying blur of flesh-rending points! Capable of delivering the kind of elevated slaughter one would almost feel honored to be on the receiving end of.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Well, my dear. You've cleaned me out. The last of my gear, and... yes, there it is. My last sardine.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: And so, with my tale told and treasures distributed, we've reached the natural end of this unburdening.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: I leave you now to your fate... FAREWELL!

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: And the caravan of concealment is on the :hero_faceless_void::hero_ursa::hero_clinkz::hero_kunkka:ing fritz again, so I'll be packing up and leaving like a common visible idiot.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Ah! But might I return for another unburdening, before yon gibbous moon is full... two... no, three... in a few months? Might I be returning in a few months with more stuff?

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: And WELL I MIGHT! FAREWELL!

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Ah, :hero_faceless_void::hero_ursa::hero_clinkz::hero_kunkka:. Let yourself out.
Drakon's Ire Gauntlets

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Oh. You're back. I already rolled up all the store blankets, I wasn't expecting you... at this hour.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: What time IS it? Am I just imagining it's three in the...

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: No, no it is. It's three in the morning.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Well! Hello. What can I help you with?

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: I'll be honest, I figured we were done here. I gave you all my priceless items. I told you my curse-mandated tragic backstory.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Ah, I see. You want to see those gauntlets over there. The Drakon's Ire. Of course you do, they're flawless.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: They're also in a glass case at the bottom of this pile of trunks I just packed.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Well, let me just unpack EVERYTHING then. Unless you wanted to come back — no.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Of course not. Right.
Drakon's Ire Helm

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: So just the gauntlets then? Good. The Drakon's Ire helm is the best part of the set, I'd rather not—

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Did I just say set? Damn.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Alright, yes, these are part of a set. The best set I own, in fact.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: It's just that — well, it's very similar to the item set I already gave you. I'd actually been hoping to find a DIFFERENT hero to give—

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Well, I see your point. How about you give me back the other one and—

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Right. Why not give EVERYTHING to you... and NOTHING to anyone else? That makes sense too.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: I suppose.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Fine, let me take down this box and... no, not there. Maybe this heavy chest... nff!  No.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Tell you what, why don't I just unpack everything.
Drakon's Ire Tassets

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: You know, I could just refuse. What's the worst that could happen?

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: In fact, I WILL refuse. No.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: I WON'T give you this AGGHHHHHH MY BONE MARROW

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Fine fine fine. Here, take the priceless tassets, they're yours.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: I hope you appreciate this little loophole you've found, double-dipper.
Drakon's Ire Pauldrons

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Let me tell you… you REMIND me of someone.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: A good person? No, hero. A real piece of shit. Someone impetuous.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Someone with no sense of decency. Someone willing to wake up a different someone at three in the gods-damn morning to shake him down for a stupid set of pauldrons.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: I take that back. These pauldrons are exquisite. I found them, by the way. Here.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Anyway, you remind me of... of...

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Well, if I'm being honest, you remind me of me.
Drakon's Ire Banners

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: You remind me of me — back before the curse, in my pre-curse days.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: My pre-quartermaster days, even. When I was a young cutpurse on the mean streets of Cladd. Oh, those were some mean streets, hero.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: For an upscale port town, I mean. Back then, the gelateria closed at 5pm and things could turn nasty.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: I ran with the Lantern Alley Boys. And I don't mind telling you, we were fast.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Candlesticks, necklaces, snuffboxes — if it wasn't nailed down, we stole it. If it WAS nailed down, we brought Hammer Pete.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Ah! Here we go. The Drakon's Ire Banners. They were just under all those heavy trunks I'd packed. It's always in the last place you'd... ever want to look.
Drakon's Ire Lance

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: I only ever got caught once. I was robbing a house so quickly I stepped on an over-varnished floor and cracked my head off a decorative bell.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Woke the whole house up. The Lord even put out a bounty on me. And do you know what I did?

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: I broke BACK into that manor at three in the morning, and stole the bounty too!

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Kind of like what you're doing now, taking and taking and taking. It feels different on this side of the counter, but I've got to tell you, hero: I respect your moxie.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Take it. Take everything. Take the Drakon's Ire Lance. No, I insist.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Until we meet again... my dear hero.
Nether Grubs

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Hero! You're BACK! And you look TERRIBLE! (Laughing) Ah, perfect!

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Look at those rags you're wearing! Come, come, get IN here!

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: I'll bet you're looking for a fresh batch of old Quartero's one-of-a-kind item sets. Well, you're... in... luck!

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Same terms as last time, you remember my tragic backstory, of course.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: The... one I spent an entire day telling you about? Yes? ...No.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Well, I suppose it was a LOT to absorb.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: In short: I'm cursed to give away item sets, for free, or I'll die.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Painfully.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Ah, I see you've got your eye on my lunch. Well, I don't have to eat it if you want it as a ward.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: You're missing out, though. I mean, I'm a goat, I'll eat anything, but still.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: (Chewing) There's a... sweet shell, some crunchy bits, a... metallic note, I think? Definitely ham. There's a lot going on here.
Nether Horn

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Here, why don't we try this Nether Horn on.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Yes yes YES. Pretty slick, am I right?

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: I managed to snag this little showstopper in a small village up in the mountains. Ruled by a SPIDER, if you can believe it.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Not a tiny spider, either... No, that would be ridiculous.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: No, a big spider, with a king's crown on its head.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: And as I'm sure you can guess, there's an adventuresome tale in how I got it.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: I was sworn to secrecy, of course.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: But, if I've learned anything about you, you're not even listening right now, so here we go.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Once upon a time...
Nether Shell

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Once upon a time... I gave you this free cape: the Nether Shell! Once owned... by the Spider King!

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Did this spider defy the odds and become a king? What an inspirational story THAT would be.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: But no. This story is about a lazy king who BECAME a spider.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: How? Well, some of the villagers said the king had been BITTEN by a spider.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Other villagers said he'd been bitten by a witch, and THAT turned him into a spider, and I asked, so was it a SPIDER-witch, then?

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: And they said no, just a regular witch, and I said well that doesn't make much sense, and they said that's funny, we didn't know you were such a :hero_faceless_void::hero_undying::hero_crystal_maiden::hero_kunkka:ing witch expert, and I was like, oh shit, I'm going to have to fight all these people.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: And then the leader said when a witch turns you into a frog does that make her a FROG-witch? And honestly, that helped me get there. You could see they'd put a... lot of thought into this.
Nether Bracers

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Ah. The Nether Bracers! Look at the craftsmanship on those spikes. That's real beetle jaw. You can tell by the way it catches the light. (Whistles) Look at that shimmer.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Anyway, while I was running from the villagers, guess who I bumped into? The king!

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: And I figured, why not just ask him how he'd become a spider, and get this: he hadn't been BITTEN by a witch, just CURSED.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: So. Mystery solved, but also who cares, because the POINT is it turned out he had an ARMOR HOARD.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: This king loved armor. A LOT. He'd spent every coin in the realm on ruinously expensive item sets. And now, thanks to the witch's curse, he couldn't wear ANY of them.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: And your old pal Quartero was thinking, how tragic.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: But also, don't... mind... if I do.
Nether Wand 1

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Here, give this Nether Wand a swing. Yes. Feel that balance? That's real cross-grained carapace steel.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Anyway, he said I could have the whole set, and he'd even throw in the wands, and all I had to do was go on a quest to the Fountain of Babrasba and find him a magic elixir. Sounded easy enough...

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: ...and then he got out the map.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: The fountain was in some tomb, in the middle of a cannibal jungle, on some godforsaken hellhole called Snake Island, and... no. Absolutely not.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Look at these hands, hero. Look at these soft, soft hands. I don't do jungle tombs.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: No hero, I had a better plan. The witch who cursed him lived five minutes from the castle. Have you ever seen a witch?

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: They're two hundred years old and they're made of balsa wood. I figured I'd just go find this witch...

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: And punch her so hard she'd die.
Nether Wand 2

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: And there's the other Nether Wand. I'm glad you're taking both, I'd hate to break up the set.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Not easy to smuggle these out of the Burrowed Kingdoms anymore, either. Not since— Well, that's another story.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Speaking of stories, where was I? Ah. Find the witch, punch her, lift the curse.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: That was the plan, anyway. As it happened, she wouldn't let me in her cottage.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: So. What I did was...

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Hmm. Let me be careful here. I... went... BACK to the village, and bought several rounds of ale at the tavern for the many witnesses present.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Yes. And WHILE I was there... you won't believe this... somebody burned her house down.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Lifted the curse instantly.
Molten Maw

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Ah, the Molten Maw. Here, lean forward, let's get this on you.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Nffh! That is HEAVY!

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: How's it feel? Can you see me out of the eyeholes?

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: You look REALLY evil, by the way. I can't tell what face you're making under there, but from here you look terrifying.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Also, legally, I feel like I should be very very clear about that last part I told you about the witch's house burning down while I was somewhere else with countless witnesses present.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: I don't think the witch is DEAD. (Chuckling) Nooo, hero. Are you kidding? That would be... murder.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: No, I think she lifted the curse, moved to a different town and changed her name.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: In fact that's almost certainly what happened. In fact that's what I told the constables.
Molten Maulers

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Anyway, I went back to the king and he was a human again! Also dead.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: I guess what happened was, he must've run straight to his armory and started trying on all his precious armor, and I guess the witch came BACK to life briefly before dying again, because he suddenly turned back into a spider, then back into a human.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: And if you suddenly go from a PERSON-shaped body into a SPIDER body, and then back into a PERSON body, while you're still inside steel armor... Well, I'll spare you the details.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: He died instantly.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: But if you WANT the details, it exploded all the vertebrae in his spine while his organs got pushed up into his throat cavity and he choked to death while his back exploded.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: And, honestly, it took a surprisingly long time. A few minutes at least.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Oh. Also, earlier... Did I say the witch came BACK from the DEAD? (Nervous chuckle) What I obviously meant... was... you look fantastic in those Molten Maulers.
Molten Mantle

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: At any rate, I can report that, unlike the witch, happily retired somewhere, I imagine, the king was dead.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: I was able to pry most of him out of this Molten Mantle here, let's get it on you, hm?

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Nffh! There! Snug as a button.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: There might still be a few chunks slopping around in there, you can keep those if you find any, the villagers and I found enough of him to bury.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: The point is, technically the king was 100% curse-free by the end, and a deal's a deal.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: So yours truly helped himself, as agreed, to any one item set of my choosing.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Naturally I chose the Nether Beetle set. But then I also liked the look of the Molten Monarch set, so I figured, why not take BOTH for now so you could try them on, and I'd return whichever one you didn't like?

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: And THAT gave me another idea, which is why not steal EVERYTHING, and I was just smashing a third set out of its glass case when some guards showed up.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Now, I'll bet you're wondering. I said at the beginning that this story had a HAPPY ending. Yet here we are at the end of the tale and the entire cast is dead or missing.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Ah! But YOU have two priceless item sets. And you lived handsomely ever after in them... the end.
Ember Mane

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Ah, the Ember Enforcer! Go ahead, try it on!

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: I know it looks like it's on fire. That is because it is on fire.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: But most of the heat radiates outward, so once you've got it on that should be the worst of the burns.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Funny story behind this item set. I actually obtained it while trying to get my hands on a different set at Ultimyr University.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: I'd tried sneaking my way into the university disguised as a professor. \"Welcome to class! You there! Read that book! Good!\" and so on.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: I hadn't counted on a Gem of True Sight, which was judging every heart in the room for so much as a flicker of ill intent.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Well, my heart must have been flickering like the dickens with shitty intentions, because I found myself in the university dungeon before I could snatch a single sabaton.
Ember Armor

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Let's get this armor on you.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Nffh! That is heavy.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: You must be roasting like a duck in there.  Well, If it gets too hot just wave.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Anyway, prison. I didn't care for it.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: I didn't like the cell. I didn't like the rats, or the bed, or the toilet next to the bed.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: But mostly I didn't like Dodrick. He was the jailer.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: I mean, I get it, it's prison, Quartero's not made of marshmallow jam. But, I mean... a simple BLANKET to keep me warm at night.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: I had one, yes, but two would have been even snugglier, and there was a whole pile of them in the linen closet.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Or the food, hero. A bowl of gruel is literally water and gristle. It would have cost the prison essentially nothing to adopt a bottomless bowl policy.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: It was like Dodrick was going out of his way to make prison as unpleasant as possible.
Ember Sigil

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Look at the glowing sigil on this backpiece!

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: You know, it's odd, when I look directly at the sigil... It's like it fills my heart with...

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Oh, what's the word I'm looking for?

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Ah! Despair. That's it. Looking at it fills me with despair.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Tell you what, I'm going to stop.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Anyway, there I was, rotting away in the dungeon, lying on my filthy mattress next to my filthy toilet, when there, on the filthy wall, I spotted it.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: A summoning spell! I could summon a GENIE!

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: I could wish that Dodrick would fall into his gruel cauldron and drown!

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: And that his death spasms knocked over the pile of spare blankets and they all rolled into my cell!

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Also I could have just wished to not be in PRISON, obviously, but I was still VERY cross with Dodrick at the time and, well, not thinking straight.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: I fudged some of the syllables here and there, but basically got the spell right, and presto!
Ember Warkilt

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Let me cinch the belt for you. There! Give the warkilt a twirl.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Yes! Very nice twirling.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Next time wear something under the warkilt, that was... a LOT for your old pal Quartero.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Where was I in my gripping prison narrative? Right! The breakout! I'd summoned a wish-granting genie!

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Genie! I commanded, \"Heed my first wish!\"

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Well, it turns out I didn't say every single little tiny syllable in the spell perfect.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Because I hadn't summoned a wish-granting genie after all, but a much rarer people-murdering genie.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: I asked if he'd let me make a wish anyway as long as it didn't involve him not murdering someone, and he said no.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: In fact, ALL he wanted to know was which insolent fool had summoned him, because he said he was going to...

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: And I quote, \"pound out their skeleton and wear their skin like a jacket.\"

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: So I said, \"It was him.\"

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: And I pointed at Dodrick.
Magma Fang

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: I saved the best for last: the Magma Fang!

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: So the best part about this weapon... other than it's a glowing axe the size of a horse, is... look closely.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: It's not even forged! It's just a massive shard of lava rock!

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: And let me tell you, it cuts through prison bars like a hot knife through a surprised jailer.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: The murder genie melted the bars, grabbed Dodrick by the ankles, and smashed him against a wall until his skeleton came out.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Now, technically my cell didn't have bars blocking the way out anymore. But it DID have a giant murder-genie in ember armor.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: And he'd just run out of people to murder, so I was hoping... he wouldn't... notice...

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: ...He noticed me.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: So. I had a murder-genie stomping towards me holding that Magma Fang, wearing poor stupid Dodrick as a jacket. My back was against the wall.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: What could I do? I said the summoning spell again.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Now I had TWO murder-genies in the room with me.
Golden Mane

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Ah, the Gilded Tyrant! Volcanically gilded with mercury, I believe.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Unbelievably toxic, of course, but it's not like you're going to put it in your mouth or anything...

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Or on your skin or near your face... So! There I was.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: I'd said the summoning spell AGAIN, and what must have been the first murder-genie's SUPERVISOR showed up, because he was wearing the same armor as the FIRST guy... except it looked a lot more expensive.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: He was also just as angry as the first guy. \"What insolent fool summoned me, I will pound out their skeleton,\" all the same stuff.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: And I figured, well, it worked once, so I point at the first genie and I say: \"HE summoned you. Kill him.\"

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Did it work?

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: (Laughing)

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: It did not.
Golden Armor

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Your eyes aren't deceiving you. Those glowing spikes on the shoulders? Oh yes. That's genuine Six-Hell crystallized brimstone.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Each spike lovingly hammered by hand.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: ...each hand lovingly attached to someone thrown screaming into a volcano, after every single spike.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Put your ear close and listen. You hear that?

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: That's right. Screams. Of pride, I imagine.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: At any rate, my clever plan was to use deception to pit the genies against each other.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: A real comedy of errors, like in those classic plays where a handsome rogue tricks two genies into killing each other, you know the ones.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Of course, in THOSE plays it only works because nobody ever stops to compare notes and clear up the misunderstanding, which unfortunately these genies did almost instantly.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Bazroth, the supervisor, and Griknok, his subordinate, hashed it all out before I was halfway to the door.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: And if there's one thing genies hate more than humans summoning them, it's apparently LYING about it.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Because they started telling me they were going to do things to my skeleton that didn't seem possible if done in sequence. They were simply going to have to pick one.
Golden Sigil

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Ah. Excellent eye, hero. I see you've zeroed in on the backpiece. That's the obsidian sigil of the Sixth Hell.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: I'm not sure which one, though. Hold on, I've got a sigil handbook around here somewhere.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Let's see... here... ah. \"Nal Vorrth Oog-MUR-toh.\" Roughly translated, \"Throw all concerns into the wind.\"

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Well that's nice. Hold on, I didn't see the umlaut over the O. Roughly translated, \"Throw all humans into the volcano.\" Hm.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Let me wrap up that gripping prison tale. Where were we? Summoning spell, Griknok the murder-genie, dead jailer, SECOND summoning spell, Bazroth the supervisor, both of them about to kill me, me and my skin out of tricks.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: All set? Here we go!

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: So there I was: out of tricks. Griknok stomped over to me and grabbed me by the throat. \"I'm going to enjoy this,\" he said.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: And hero? I believed him. He looked like he was about to have the time of his life.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: But then Bazroth said, \"Oh no, you don't. You know the rules.\" And Griknok grumbled and stepped aside, and then BAZROTH puts his hands around my throat.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: And I thought, \"the rules\"?  THIS might be useful.
Golden Warkilt

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Ahh. I see your gaze has fallen on the Golden Warkilt of Ugmörto.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Your eyes have fine taste, hero. Smelted in magma drawn from the Six-Hell caldera, and cooled in the blood of the poor souls who made the shoulder spikes.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: See that belt sigil? That's not ornamentation, that's a containment rune.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Nothing evil, it just... well, you know. Keeps everything contained down there.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: So. Why COULDN'T Griknok kill me?

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: A very good question, and I needed a way to subtly insert it into the conversation, so I asked: \"Hey, why can't Griknok kill me?\"

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Well, according to Bazroth, every genie is allowed to kill whoever summoned them. That's the rule.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: And because I'd told Griknok that stupid smelly Dodrick had summoned him, Griknok got to kill stupid smelly Dodrick.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: I'd summoned Bazroth, so Bazroth got to kill me. I guess that's why it was the first thing both of them asked.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: So I said, actually: I lied.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: I summoned Griknok. I'd done ALL the summoning so far. They'd killed stupid smelly Dodrick for nothing.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: And the genies didn't say ANYTHING after that, for a long long time.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: And then Griknok said \"Shit.\"

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: And then Bazroth, after a while, he also said \"Shit.\"
Gilded Fang

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Presenting the Gilded Fang!

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Forged in the black fires of the Six-Hell Caldera, where only the heaviest metals survive.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Hauled from the very throat of the vent, its edge cast and hardened in a cataclysm of molten stone and threaded with vein-gold from the mantle of the Sixth Hell.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: And that's a lot of technical mumbo-jumbo, but the gist is this axe is cool as hell and it's yours for free.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: I'll also throw in the thrilling conclusion to my prison tale. Both the genies seemed to think they were in a LOT of trouble, and they were begging me to sign some contract they'd written up on Dodrick's skin stating that Dodrick had summoned both of them.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: I gave the contract a once-over. It didn't look like there were any clauses hidden away in the fine print, so I added some.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: After all, I'd come to Ultimyr looking for some gear to steal, and then these two idiots show up wearing Six-Hell caldera armor. The shoulder guards alone were worth more than the entire university.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: So I told them I'd sign on one condition: that both of them immediately get nude.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Griknok looked confused and a little scared, and wanted to know if he could ask why before he said yes. And I said calm down, I just want your armor, now take your clothes off.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: And hero? Take their clothes off they did. Stripped right down. Griknok was a little shyer about it than Bazroth. For good reason as it turned out.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: After which I signed the contract, sent them on their way back to Six-Hell, and here I am, giving the spoils... to you.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: I hope the harrowing story of their acquisition increases their value in your eyes, knowing as you now do the trials I undertook to get them t— No, I didn't think so. Weren't even listening, were you?

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: No, it's fine, it's late. Take it. I will see you in a few months.
Antique Intro

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Last time I came around I made sure to give everyone some chances to win free stuff, and the response was unanimous! Every single person was mad.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: So! This time Quartero's going to make sure your first antique is an extra super-duper special one.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Then it's back to the usual stuff. But! You'll get more chances to win it.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Last but not least! Now you'll get to pick your treasure from an assortment of options.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Happy? Everybody... finally happy with how I'm giving away all my stuff? Super.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Anybody with further suggestions can mail them directly to Quartero at One Two Three Kiss My Purple Ass Lane.
Lotus Calyx

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: Oh. Hello.

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: Are you a friend of my brother's? Or are you breaking into his safehouse?

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: Or are you a friend of my brother's AND you're breaking into his safehouse?

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: I suppose it doesn't matter. That armor you're stealing is called the Lotus Calyx, by the way.

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: And I'll admit, it looks like it was made for you.

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: Knowing my brother, there's a good chance you're stealing it BACK from him.

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: In any case, keep it. Have you SEEN my brother, by the way?

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: He told me to meet him here, and his letter made it sound urgent.

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: Which means someone's trying to kill him again.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: SISTER! Quintessa, you're not—

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Oh, hello Hero. That armor looks really terrific on you.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Quintessa, you're not going to believe this, but someone is trying to kill me!
Lotus Binding

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Hero, will you please take this Lotus Binding? Ceremonial waistpiece, made from a living silk spun by the oracle-worms of Pran. I insist you have it.

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: It does look nice.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: That's exactly why I'm insisting.

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: Brother, why do you keep giving this man free armor?

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Have I not told you about my curse?

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: Is this the one where your tongue falls out if you lie?

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: What? No, I got that absolved by a ghost pirate captain AGES ago.

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: Oh, that's right.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: QUITE an adventuresome tale as well, I don't mind telling you.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: In fact, why DON'T I tell you.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: There I was, in a sinking rowboat off Smuggler's Reach—

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: Brother. Focus.
Lotus Crown

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: You were telling me about your curse, brother.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Right. The curse I'm saddled with these days is giving this hero here priceless item sets or my bone marrow turns into bugs.

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: You're joking.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Boiling worms, I think. I'll be honest, I try not to let the curse get so far along that I get a close look.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Speaking of... the Lotus Crown. Ceremonial headpiece.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Also alive, I believe. Whispers to you if you wear it long enough.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Eventually burrows itself into your head.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Step back a moment and let me get a look at you.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Hmmm. Yes.

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: Oh, very much yes. Hero, do not give that back.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Maybe don't wear it full time, though. The burrowing.
Lotus Veil

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: Quartero, why is someone trying to kill you? Did you STEAL from him?

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: No!

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Wait, did you say \"steal\"? Oh. Yes. A LOT.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Every item set in this safehouse, really.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Speaking of, Hero, that piece you can't take your eyes off of is the Lotus Veil.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Here, let me help you get it on. NFF.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Oh, that looks marvellous.

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: Brother. WHO is trying to kill you?

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: You promise you won't get mad when I tell you?

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: I promise.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Blake Sextus.

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: Master thief Blake Sextus? Engine of revenge Blake Sextus? Last thing you see in a dark room Blake Sextus?

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: (Nervous Laughter)

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: Hero, does that item set come with a weapon? If so, you can save some time and kill us both with it.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: It doesn't, no. It does come with a swarm of bugs, though, I suppose they could kill us in a pinch.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Where did I put... that swarm... of... bugs... Ah!
Lotus Swarm

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: The Lotus Swarm!

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: One swarm of killer bugs, as promised.

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: So THAT'S where you've been these last few months. Finding a steady supply of priceless item sets to give away to this hero here.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: This ungrateful hero, yes. Not so much as a thank you, I hope you've noticed.

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: I did notice that. Just takes and takes without a word of gratitude, it seems like.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: You're not alone in noticing.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Anyway, I put out feelers around White Spire that I was a master criminal.

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: But you aren't a master criminal.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: I am not, but I'm an EXCELLENT liar.
Lotus Spirits

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Sister, while I delve into my current predicament, would you mind handing Hero those Lotus Spirits over there? I can feel the curse coming on a touch.

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: Here you are, Hero.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Thank you. Where was I? Right. I'd put out feelers that I was a retired master criminal with a poor legless child.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Or possibly a kidneyless wife, I can't remember now who didn't have what, but one of them was VERY sick, and wouldn't you know it, I'd been pulled back into a life of super-crime for one last job.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Three days later, I came back to my room at the Black Barb Inn, and guess who was sitting in the dark, calmly smoking a cigarette?

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: I hope it was Blake Sextus, or this story is going to go on forever.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: It WAS Blake Sextus, and this story is about to get riveting, I promise you.
The Boltspire

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Ah, the Boltspire.

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: Hold on. You're giving them a crown that's already theirs?

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: No no, it wasn't Hero's until just now.

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: Really. Because it looks like it was MADE for them.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: It does, doesn't it.

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: So: Blake Sextus had broken into your room and was smoking a calm cigarette.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: He was. And the REASON he was —

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: The reason he was in my room, I mean, not the reason he was smoking a cigarette calmly in the dark, I assume that was to look cool...

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: Did he?

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: I mean—Hero, sister, don't take up smoking! But yes.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Anyway, the reason he was in my room was to offer me a job.

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: One last job?

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Of course. And then he was out for good.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: The mausoleum score. A mausoleum FULL of priceless armor sets, guarded by riddles.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: He said he needed a riddlemaster. And I said he had his man.

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: But you're not a riddlemaster.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: He did not know that.
The Thunderhand

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Let's give you the Thunderhand Bracers to go with that Crown. I'd hate to break up the set.

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: Amazing. And you're sure you didn't STEAL this from Hero here? You're not just giving it BACK to him?

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: I swear to you, it just LOOKS like it was made for them. Where was I?

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: The Mausoleum Score.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: The Mausoleum Score! The next night, I met Blake Sextus at Grimwood Estate — the home of Galdron the dark sorcerer.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Galdron lived inside an enormous black obelisk in the center of the estate.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: No doors or windows whatsoever — which was perfect, since he wouldn't be able to see us stealing all his shit out of his backyard.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Every dark sorcerer who’d ever owned Grimwood Estate had been buried out back, like a family dog. Interred with their best armor in the estate's mausoleum.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Barely guarded at all, according to Blake, because of the riddles.

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: Which he thought you could solve, for some reason.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Which I lied to him that I COULD solve. So for that reason.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Anyway, not only was the mausoleum unguarded, it was completely unlocked.

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: The sorcerer forgot to lock it!

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: No, sister, there WERE no locks.

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: Oh. Hm. That is OMINOUS.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Well, you should have been there. You could have warned us.
The Oathbinder

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Sister, could you hand Hero there the Oathbinder? I don't want to lose my place in the story.

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: There you are.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: So there we were, in the vestibule of the mausoleum. I was approaching the stairs down to the burial chamber when Blake stopped me and pointed at a portrait on the wall.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: It was a painting of an evil old man. I assume he owned the place at some point.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: And it was LOOKING AROUND.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Blake said to hand him my bottomless bag of holding. I said absolutely not, then I'd have no reason to be here, and he said, of course you would, you're the riddle master, and I said, oh right, my mastery of riddles.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: And then he said, as long as you're going to prattle on like that, go do it in front of the painting, and he pushed me out in front of it.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: So the painting bellows \"WHO GOES THERE!\"

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: And I said, \"Oh, hello,\" and tried not to look at Blake Sextus sidling up against the wall, which I failed at doing.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: \"What are you looking at?\" the painting asked. What I was looking at was a very annoyed Blake Sextus making a \"keep talking\" duck quack motion with his hand.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: So I did! And while the portrait was waiting for its turn to talk, Blake crept up beside it and pushed it off its nail into my bottomless bag of holding.
The Skybearer

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Where was I? Oh! We'd gotten there! To the burial chamber with all the item sets I'm giving Hero here!

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Here's the Skybearer, by the way. Sister, can you grab an end? This thing is ENORMOUS.

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: Hero, don't move, we're going to have to drop it suddenly onto your shoulders...

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: ...THERE. Four hundred sudden pounds of weight on your shoulders.

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: Brace yourself.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Yes. That's exactly what we should have told him to do. Anyway, here's the story of how I stole it.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Imagine, Sister -- and Hero, you can also imagine this -- a vast cathedral, with statues of creepy old wizards as far as the eye could see. And on every one, a priceless set of armor!

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: My hand was already outstretched to pluck the first gauntlet off an arm, when Blake once again stopped me.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: We hid behind one of the statues. Blake reached out to the gauntlet I'd been about to grab, and NUDGED one of the fingers a single little inch.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Almost immediately, a shape emerged from a fountain in the middle of the chamber. It congealed into a body, and slopped toward us.

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: A water golem?

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Indeed. A real nasty-looking :hero_faceless_void::hero_undying::hero_crystal_maiden::hero_kunkka:er too. It walked right up to us... reached out...

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: ...And pushed the finger of the gauntlet back to its original position. With that, it returned to the fountain. I started breathing again.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Blake nodded, took a bag out of his backpack...

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: And filled the fountain with quick drying cement.
The Berserker's Bloodplate

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: The portrait, the water golem -- Blake must have been researching this place for months!

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: He'd only made one small mistake the entire night: His assumption of my baseline competence as a riddlemaster. As we are all about to find out.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Because, just as I made a grab for an item set, one of the statues came to life.

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: Oh...

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Anyway, he said \"Answer thee my riddles three, or here shalt thou forever be.\"

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: And Blake said, \"Alright, riddlemaster, you're up.\"

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: And I said, \"Fair enough... let's see here... 'thou shalt not'... or was it 'here shalt thou'?\"

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: I asked the gatekeeper if he could repeat this tricky first riddle, and let me tell you, if a statue can look confused, this one did.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: It clarified it hadn't actually gotten to the riddles yet. And I said, \"I see.\" And Blake looked worried.
The Berserker's Gore-Greaves

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Sister, could you be a lamb and hand Hero these Berserker's Gore-Greaves? I'm feeling a little crampy, I think it's the curse acting up again.

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: Here you go, Hero.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Ah, that's better.

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: What WAS the first riddle, anyway?

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Oh, just some nonsense, I don't even think it had an answer. Let's see, what was it? Uhh...

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: \"Far from land it haunts the sea, footless still, yet roaming free; wingless borne, yet it doth fly— Speak its name, and answer I.\"

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: Ship. It's a ship.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Ha! Funny that you say that, that's what Blake thought too. Kept screaming \"SHIP!\" at the top of his lungs.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Anyway, I went with \"footless ghost\".

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Then the gatekeeper said that was wrong, and that we were now both trapped in the mausoleum for eternity, and that's when all the dead ancestors started coming to life, and the doors started closing, and Blake REALLY started screaming at me.
Clot

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Ah, Clot the shield. The last line of defense.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: What you'd absolutely want to hold in front of you if, to pick a random example, a mausoleum full of angry mummies was about to tear you apart like a wet head of lettuce.

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: So how did you get away?

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Well. Have you ever heard the maxim, 'I don't need to outrun the bear, I just need to outrun you'?

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: Yes.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Well, I don't know if you've seen Blake Sextus's calf muscles, but the man is carved from oak, so there was no way I was outrunning him.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: So. There was Blake, about to sprint quickly AWAY from the danger, and me, much slower, about to be killed by it.

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: So what did you do?

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: What COULD I do? My hands were tied. I grabbed a heavy bronze ornamental scepter, I really wound up with it...

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: ...and I hit him in the leg.

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: So what did HE do?

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: I fell over with a broken leg.

messages.speaker: Quartero & Quintessa
messages.text: Oh shit, Blake Sextus!

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: And then I watched you clop over to the closest item sets.

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: And stuff them in your bottomless bag of holding.

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: Then you pointed at me and told the zombies \"Kill him!\"

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: Then you whispered \"I'm so sorry.\"

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: And you rolled under the door just before it closed.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Ah good. So you remember my apology.
Cut

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: Quartero Quickhoof...

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: Here I thought I'd have to torture you until you told me where the loot was.

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: And I find you standing in a room with it.

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: Giving it all to this idiot for some reason.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Oh, I don't think I'm doing that, exactly.

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: You're doing it right now. You're giving that idiot a priceless weapon.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: I think you're mistaken.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Here, take Blake Sextus's priceless weapon, don't tell him I gave this to you.

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: Stop that!
Wyrmsbane

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: Would you stop giving this idiot my treasure while I'm trying to kill you?

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: You! Take my armor off!

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Here, hero, take these bracers.

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: You're still doing it!

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: I need to or I'll die!

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: HELLO, what's this?

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: What IS that?

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: I think it's a SCROLL.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: It was folded up. It must have been tucked into the sleeve of those bracers.

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: A scroll? That's mine too.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: It's an OPENING SPELL to Galdron the sorcerer's vault.

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: GIVE... THAT... TO ME.

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: Brother! Don't give it to him!

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: What are you doing? Do not put that in your mouth!

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: (Gobbling Sound)

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: I will strangle you and cut it out of you! Right in front of your sister and the hero!

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: (Chewing Sounds)

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: Are you chewing? DO NOT SWALLOW THAT, you son of a--

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: (Swallowing Sound)
SurpentKoil

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: There. You can cut the pulpy wad out of me if you like.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: But if you want that spell of vault opening, I'm afraid you're going to have to ask.

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: ...can I... can I have the spell?

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: No.

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: Look. You can keep all this crap from the mausoleum score.

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: Hand it to this idiot as much as you like.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: I WILL hand this crap to this idiot. Here you go, idiot. And it's not crap by the way.

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: No. It's NOT. In fact it's PRICELESS. That's SurpentKoil armor. It was worn by a GOD.

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: And it's all yours. Everything in this room.

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: Plus I won't kill you for doublecrossing me. All I want is that open spell.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Sold. Do you have a pen? MASCUS... PARIAH...

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: Whoa whoa whoa.

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: Brother. Think for a moment.

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: If he's willing to give us everything in this room for whatever's in Galdron's vault...

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: ...ah. Then what's in the VAULT must be even MORE priceless.
Wulfward

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: Alright, new plan. We're going back to Galdron's palace.

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: And we're breaking into his impenetrable Obelisk.

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: \"Impenetrable\" means...

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: I know what it means. We're breaking in anyway.

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: And then we're breaking into his vault, with the spell that's in your head.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Alright, but I want sixty percent.

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: You want seventy percent.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: We want eighty percent.

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: Look. You two. I want what's in the sorcerer's vault SLIGHTLY more than I want to kill you.

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: But don't push it.
Reckoner

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: We're gonna need a riddle master.

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: I'm a riddle master.

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: Nice try. Your brother already pulled that grift on me.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: No, she actually is! She went to riddle college! That's where I got the idea!

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: It's true! Go on! Ask me any riddle!

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: What is blue and purple and never shuts up.

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: Easy, that's us. My turn. What's pushy and insulting and should be a little nicer if it wants our help breaking into Galdron's vault?

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: Fine. You're my riddle master.

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: You. Hero.

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: This is the Reckoner. It's the most valuable piece we took from the mausoleum.

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: It's what I came looking for. It's what I was gonna kill this idiot to take BACK.

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: It's yours. You're gonna need it. You're the muscle on this score.

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: And you. Idiot.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Yes?

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: Unfortunately, you're my safe cracker. DONT. FORGET. THAT. SPELL.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Don't worry about me, I've got it memorized. MASCUS... PARIAH...

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: Brother.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Right.

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: We'll meet south of Galdron's place in three turns of the broken moon.

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: There's something I need to get first.
Antique Intro

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Welcome back to Quartero's Curios! The quarterly... quarterly-ish?

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Who am I kidding, this is Valve, the REGULAR feature where I give you all-new item sets and chances at classic antiques, all for free, and all for doing what you do best: Playing Dota.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Oh! Let me check with the team quick and see if there are any new announcements for this season.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Ah, here we are: \"Duplicate Protection!\"

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Sometimes when you get five antique options, two of them might be the same.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Apparently they fixed that. Nice work, everyone. Anything else?

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Last thing: Evidently some of you have been playing long enough that you own... a LOT of shit.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: So sometimes when you do your antique pull you'll already own everything.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Not much we can do about that, unless you want us to start deleting your inventory so you get the thrill of the chase back.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: No, I didn't think you'd like that. Anyway, now you get shards.
Living Ingot

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Hero! You found us! Oh, you're a sight for sore bone marrow.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: I've been waiting for you to show up. Quintessa and Blake are up ahead looking for a way into the obelisk.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: I tried giving THEM item sets while you were gone, but it's like the curse KNOWS they're not heroic enough.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: No, if anyone's getting magnificent item sets, absolutely free, just for breathing, I'm afraid it has to be you.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Speaking of. Let's see what I've got in my bag of holding here... ah!

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: The Golden Orbweaver! Perfect.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Here, don't take the whole set at once. Just take the Living Ingot...

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Slowly now... slower... I'm giving you the livinnnnng innnngot... for nooooo monnnney...

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Ahh. Curse lifted. For now, anyway.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: These are the LAST item sets from the mausoleum heist, by the way. We'll need to make these last until we get inside Galdron's vault.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Let's go find the others. I hope Blake found a way into this obelisk, or my bone marrow is in some real trouble here.
Mournless Mask

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Blake, Quintessa! Look who I found!

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: Shh! Quiet! What took you so long?

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Well, we did stop for a minute so I could give them some armor.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Also, here you go, Hero. The Mournless Mask — segmented carapax plates, sleeved beneath a lacquered chitin carapace!

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: Wait. Brother, is your bone marrow turning into bugs ALREADY? You said you gave Hero an item when they got here.

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: Is your curse speeding up?

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Oh, I wouldn't say THAT.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: The intervals between the times where I need to give Hero free items to make the pain stop are... are SHRINKING, yes, but...

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: Shut up about your curse. I found us a way in.

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: Hide the horses. We'll go the rest of the way on foot.
Gilded Tarsi

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Here you go, Hero. The Gilded Tarsi.

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: Hey! Shut up back there.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Shutting up back here.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: It's fully segmented, reverse-hinged blackened alloy.

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: I said shut up back there.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: I was just about to! And now I am. There.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: I think that's real moons-cured obsidian, too.

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: Chatty goat. If I have to come back there and shut you up, you are not gonna like how I do it.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: I'm sure I won't.

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: No. You won't. Because first I'll take those horns of yours, I'll snap 'em off, and I'll kick 'em both so far up—

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: You're painting an INCREDIBLY vivid word picture. I promise. Not... another... word.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Moons-cured obsidian. You look marvellous.
Captive's Crown

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: Everyone, get over here. I want to show you something.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Coming!

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: The Captive Crown. Here, take it.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: And before you can tell me to shut up, Blake, I'm shutting up.

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: Good.

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: Welcome to Grimwood Estate. Home of Galdron the Sorcerer.

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: Let's not forget Galdron the Sorcerer's vault full of treasure.

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: Let's not get ahead of ourselves. See that up there? That's a sentry.

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: Awwww! It's a little koi pond.

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: Don't look in it. It's a trap.

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: It doesn't look like a trap. It looks... like a koi pond.

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: You're still looking at it. Stop looking at it!

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: I've been looking at it the whole time you've been talking and nothing has happened.

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: I'm still looking at it too. I can see fish swimming in it.

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: Hmph. Don't look INTO it.

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: Those scrying ponds are his EYES. He can sit in that obelisk and monitor the whole estate from up there.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: That doesn't make sense. Wouldn't he just be looking up at the sky?

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: The pond reflects at an angle.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: He could just look out his windows. If he'd bothered to install any.

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: It's a terrible design, isn't it. He must be breathing his own skin up there.

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: You, don't look in the pond. You, shut up about breathing skin.
Skittering Plague

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: OK, hero, you heard Blake. Let's do this quietly. And NOT in front of a koi pond... apparently.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Here. The Skittering Plague.

messages.speaker: Quartero
messages.text: Disgusting, aren't they? Millions of the godsdamn things. All yours.

messages.speaker: Quintessa
messages.text: Oh, they're adorable. Look at their cute little eyeballs!

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: Everybody shut up. Stop giving each other item sets for five seconds and gather round.

messages.speaker: Sextus
messages.text: This obelisk was built ten thousand years ago by an insane chthonic architect named Balthazar Blackspire.

messages.speaker: Sextus
